Roles
HardRole guide

Jungle

The map's playmaker: farm the wilds, gank lanes, and control every big objective.

You'll enjoy this role if…

  • You like making decisions and deciding where the action happens.
  • You'd rather roam the whole map than stay in one lane.
  • You enjoy reading the game and guessing what the enemy will do next.
  • You like having a big impact on all your teammates' games.

What this role does

The jungler doesn't have a lane. Instead, you farm the monster camps between the lanes, surprise enemy laners with ganks, and lead your team in taking dragons, Void Grubs, Rift Herald and Baron.

  • Clear jungle camps efficiently to keep up in gold and experience.
  • Gank lanes where a kill or a flash is likely.
  • Track the enemy jungler and warn your lanes.
  • Control objectives: dragons, Void Grubs, Rift Herald and Baron.
  • Counter-gank: show up when the enemy jungler attacks your lanes.

How the jungle works

As a jungler you take Smite, which deals big damage to monsters, and you start with a jungle pet item: Scorchclaw Pup (damage), Gustwalker Hatchling (speed) or Mosstomper Seedling (tankiness). The pet helps you clear and grows by killing monsters.

Junglers take 50% less damage from normal monsters, and killing large monsters restores some health. Still, the jungle wears you down, so use your health potions and recall when needed.

The camps you'll clear:

CampFirst spawnRespawn
Blue Sentinel, Red Brambleback0:555:00
Murk Wolves, Raptors0:552:15
Gromp, Krugs1:072:15
Rift Scuttler (river crab)2:552:30

Blue buff gives ability haste and mana regeneration. Red buff makes your attacks burn and slow, and heals you out of combat. Killing a Scuttler leaves a Speed Shrine in that river for 90 seconds, which gives vision and speed.

Your first clear and the jungle quest

Your first route through the jungle is called your first clear. A common one is a full clear: all six camps on your side, starting at one buff and ending near the river around 3:00, in time to fight for the Scuttler or gank a lane. Faster champions can start at a buff, take three camps, and gank early.

Your laners help you with the first camp (the leash). Ask for one in chat or with a ping before the game starts.

The jungle role quest is completed by feeding your pet: it needs 35 stacks from monsters. When it's done, you get:

  • Primal Smite, the strongest version of Smite.
  • +10 gold and +10 experience for each large camp.
  • Bonus move speed in the jungle and river (4%, or 8% out of combat).
Pro tipStart your clear at the buff on the side where your lane is stronger. If your bot lane is winning, end your clear near bot so you can gank there with a level advantage.

Pathing and ganking

Pathing means choosing which camps to clear and where to go next. Good junglers plan ahead: "I'll clear these three camps, then gank mid when the enemy mid uses Flash."

Gank a lane when:

  • The enemy laner is pushed up toward your side, far from their tower.
  • The enemy has used Flash or their escape ability.
  • Your laner has crowd control to help (a stun, root or slow).
  • The enemy laner is low on health.

Don't gank when the enemy is under their tower with full health and Flash, or when you'd waste a lot of time walking there. Every failed gank is lost farm.

Walk in through fog of war and avoid known enemy wards. Coming in from behind the enemy (around their side of the lane) is often best, because they have to run past you.

Common mistakeDon't spend the whole early game ganking one losing lane. If a lane is far behind and the enemy has vision, help a lane that can actually win instead, or farm and take objectives.

Objective control

Objectives are the jungler's main job after the early game:

  • Dragons spawn at 5:00 and return 5:00 after each kill. Each drake gives your team a permanent buff, and the first team to 4 gets the Dragon Soul. After a team gets Soul, the Elder Dragon appears 6:00 later. Its buff burns enemies and executes them below 20% health.
  • Void Grubs: 3 grubs spawn at 8:00 in the top pit (one wave only, gone at 14:45). Each grub makes your team stronger against turrets, and all three summon little Voidmites while you hit structures.
  • Rift Herald spawns at 15:00 and leaves at 19:45. Ride her into a turret for 3000 true damage.
  • Baron Nashor spawns at 20:00 and returns 6:00 after each kill. Hand of Baron makes your team and nearby minions much stronger for 3 minutes.

Set up objectives about a minute early: push your lanes, place wards, and get your team there first. Read Objectives: Dragons, Grubs, Herald and Baron for the full plan. Use the Objective Timers tool (under Tools) to track respawns.

Mid and late game

After laning ends, the jungler becomes the team's tempo-setter. Keep farming your camps between fights, because a jungler with no gold can't do anything. Then show up for every objective with your team.

Smite matters a lot late in the game: keep it ready for Baron and Elder Dragon, and never use it on a small camp right before an objective. A stolen Baron can lose a game.

In fights, your job depends on your champion: tanks like Amumu start fights, while damage dealers like Master Yi wait to clean up. Junglers are also great at catching enemies who walk alone into fog.

Advanced tips

  • Track the enemy jungler. If you see them top at 3:00, they're probably not bot at 3:15. Ping your bot lane that it's safe, or go take something on the opposite side. See Tracking the Enemy Jungler.
  • Look for lanes with priority. A laner who can push their wave first can follow you to the river. Fighting near those lanes is much safer.
  • Counter-gank. If the enemy jungler ganks your lane, be there to turn the fight around.
  • Trade objectives. If the enemy takes dragon and you can't contest, take Void Grubs or a turret on the other side.
  • Use Faelights. A ward placed on a Faelight gets extra vision range. They're great spots for objective setup. See Advanced Vision Control.

Beginner-friendly champions

WarwickHeals constantly, easy clear, and his passive shows you where to gank low-health enemies.
AmumuSimple tank with a huge area stun ultimate that wins teamfights.
ViPoint-and-click ultimate makes ganks reliable and easy to land.
Jarvan IVStrong early ganks and a combo that's simple to learn.
Master YiFast farmer who teaches you clear routes. Great at cleaning up fights.

Common mistakes

  • Ganking a lane that's pushed under the enemy tower, then falling behind on farm.
  • Forgetting your camps: a jungler who only ganks ends up poor and weak.
  • Using Smite on a small camp right before dragon or Baron spawns.
  • Starting objectives without vision or without your lanes pushed.
  • Following one losing lane for 15 minutes instead of playing where you can win.
  • Arguing with laners about ganks instead of pinging and moving on.
